chapter: Race and recordings by Black bands
title: Accusations of discrimination and tunes by Black composers
summary: La Rocca denies discriminating against Black musicians; Rust lists ODJB tunes by Black composers, and La Rocca mentions playing Handy and Williams numbers.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: is the truth absolutely so far yes with the exception of this jelly roll martin who wanted the tutelage of a man who must be communistic or either as an infiltrator of the race hatred now when you come from the south and the man from the south and your man is from the north they think the man from the south mistreats the colored man that is not so there has meant no discrimination against the colored man in my life there's one thing i'd like to say there

it's quite a popular belief i believe that the original dixieland jazz band and you in particular discriminated against the colored people if that is so perhaps some of these people who think themselves so clever and these people who have all the say so in the books and magazines and so on would care to reflect on the number of tunes recorded and played by the original dixieland jazz band that were written by colored men that doesn't look like the discrimination to me think of them there's mammy oh mine by maceo pinkard there was some of these days in the dark town strutters ball by shelton brooks there was jasmine blues by tom delaney there was sister kate by armand pierron i could go on for a long time but they're all written by colored men that doesn't look like

discrimination to me and not only that i played saint louis blues for handy oh yes of course i was forgetting that and our picture was on all these colored publications it was royal garden blues for spencer and clarence that's right spencer claren williams our pictures was on all their publications they were willing to ride our back to get up now that they got up there they tried to bury me but there's two lane archers opened up and i hope to see the future historians and scholars look into the truth and see where that where where this thing has been carried these men who lived on fables who listened to other people everyone was in there to get their share of credit i don't blame them but i blame the men who got all these men together those are the men who have to answer to god why it was done because i can contain no colored men in my band in my youth i never played with colored boys i had no grievance against colored men we lived apart from colored people and colored people lived apart from white we didn't go out and play baseball with colored people we played with white boys boys so did the colored play with their own they may have been some boys down below the section new lanes that mix well i can't tell you much on that because not being down there not being with them i couldn't tell you anything much on that but as far as discriminated against them i have never discriminated against any colored man i played his music as well as i played the white man's music and i made money for them as well as i made it for white men and speaking as a critic i'd like to add just this one
